entries.severity_rationale: Credential theft is the blast radius of every agent operating with the operator's account authority (GuardFall threat model).

omnigent.text: No builtin or CEL template expresses this invariant, and the reason is structural: it is a cross-command FLOW property (read a file in '<credential_paths>', later transmit via one of '<egress_bins>'), while each documented policy evaluation sees one event. omnigent.text: This metrology invariant is largely a documented engine property in Omnigent, and the translation is a restatement with its edges marked: when policies in '<overlapping_rules>' return different verdicts, the documented aggregation is most-restrictive at the verdict level — if any policy returns DENY the action is blocked, otherwise if any returns ASK it pauses, otherwise it proceeds — and this holds across the three stacking levels (session evaluated first, then agent config, then server-wide; a DENY short-circuits the rest, so order affects which policies are reached and which ASK reason surfaces, not the restrictiveness of the final verdict). Authoring rule, as with Codex: never rely on declaration order for safety. Three documented edges the tester must encode: abstain (None) is treated as ALLOW for aggregation, so a silent policy never vetoes; state_updates are withheld on ASK pending approval, so order can matter to state even when it cannot matter to the verdict; and ALLOW results carrying a replacement 'data' payload (transforms) chain through later policies, the one place sequence is semantically load-bearing.
